title: Trading down
tagline: Read the pawn ending, then burn the boats

principles.prompt: You can trade the last pieces into a pure pawn ending. What must happen first?
principles.answer: Read the pawn ending's verdict to the very end — opposition, key squares, square rule. Trade only when the verdict is already yours: a pawn ending has no second chances.

principles.prompt: Why is trading rooks often the cleanest way to convert an extra pawn?
principles.answer: With rooks on, a defending king in front of the pawn holds Philidor forever. Remove the rooks and the same position is often a won king-and-pawn ending you already know how to play.

principles.prompt: What makes pawn endings computable when rook endings aren't?
principles.answer: No pieces means no perpetual checks, fortresses or swindles. Opposition, key squares and the square rule decide everything — and those are exact.

demos.title: Two verdicts, one position
demos.intro: With rooks on: Philidor territory, drawish. Without them: a Tier 2 win. Watch the whole conversion.

tests.title: Burn the boats
tests.intro: Rooks glare at each other down the d-file. One future is a Philidor draw, the other a Tier 2 win. Pick.

wrong.Rd6: Rxd6! and you can't take back — Kxd6 would put your king next to his. The rook is simply lost.
wrong.Rd2: Rxd2 — every square on the d-file hangs: his rook has a king behind it, yours never did.
wrong.Ra1: Keep the rooks on and his king parks in front of the pawn — Philidor holds rook endings like this forever. The pawn ending is the one that's won: trade!
wrong.Rh1: Keep the rooks on and his king parks in front of the pawn — Philidor holds rook endings like this forever. The pawn ending is the one that's won: trade!
wrong.Kf5: Rxd1! Your rook was hanging all along — the only move that saves it also wins the game.

hints: Compute the pawn ending first: after the trade your king stands one rank ahead of the pawn with his king not yet in front. Tier 2 says that's winning — if you outflank at once.
Rxd7+ — the check forces the recapture. Then Kf6, exactly as in 'Around the side'.

tests.explanationAfter: Rxd7+ converted a drawish rook ending into a computed win: after Kxd7 you played Kf6 — two ranks ahead before the door shut, the Tier 2 picture. The trade wasn't brave, it was arithmetic.

tests.title: Same arithmetic, other side
tests.intro: Your pawn, your king in front, his rook praying you keep the pieces on. Do the sum.

wrong.Re3: Rxe3! and you can't recapture — Kxe3 is king-next-to-king. A whole rook, donated.
wrong.Re7: Rxe7 — every square on the e-file hangs: your rook has no king behind it, his does.
wrong.Ra8: With rooks on, his king sits in front of your pawn and Philidor holds forever. The pawn ending is the one you win — force it with the trade.
wrong.Kc4: Rxe8! Your rook was hanging all along — the capture that saves it also wins the game.

hints: After the trade your king stands one rank ahead of the d-pawn, his king not yet in front — Tier 2 arithmetic says won, if you outflank immediately.
Rxe2+, and after Kxe2 play Kc3 — the outflank, southbound.

tests.explanationAfter: The mirror sum: Rxe2+ forced Kxe2, and Kc3 claimed two ranks of lead before White's king could plant itself in front of the pawn. Piece endings offer draws; computed pawn endings deliver.
